claims.statement: Tom Allen's saloon on Washington avenue was called the Champion's Rest.
claims.excerpt:

ington avenue

claims.statement: New York rivals spread a report that Tom Allen had challenged Jem Mace and that Mace had accepted; the paper says this was a scheme and not true.
claims.excerpt: to the effect that he had challenged Mace,

claims.statement: The paper says Allen wanted to strengthen the opinion that he would never again enter the ring.
claims.excerpt: by the assertion that he will never again enter the squared circle

claims.statement: Ed O'Baldwin, the Irish giant, wanted Tom Allen to travel with him giving sparring exhibitions across the country, and Allen declined.
claims.excerpt:
is desirous that Allen should travel with him and
give sparring exhibitions throughout the country

claims.statement: Tom Allen was well off financially and had a good business he was anxious to attend to.
claims.excerpt:
is well fixed financially, has a good busi-
ness, which he is anxious to attend to

claims.statement: Tom Allen has a family to care for.
claims.excerpt:
which he is anxious to attend to, and a fam-
ily to care for

claims.statement: The paper says the ring will hold neither attraction nor terror for Tom Allen in the future.
claims.excerpt:
the ring will neither have attractions
nor terrors for him in the future

notes: Interview report by the paper; Allen's denial is paraphrased, not quoted. Hint named 'Ned O'Baldwin'; the text says 'Ed. O’ Baldwin'. O'Baldwin's prison term is the paper's detail about him, not extracted.
